title: Crash debris analysed as aluminum and barium, matching Brown's Winterhaven proposal
summary: Jesse Michels tells of Crash debris analysed as aluminum and barium, matching Brown's Winterhaven proposal, about 1950s-1960 at United States (no place named), and frames it as the host. As told, not a fact.

tellings.quote: And where have we seen barium before? Both on the chalkboard at the Bownson labs where Townsend Brown worked and in his Winterhaven proposal. Brown brings up barium to be used in one of his motors for his gravitator discs.

plain: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, in a documentary about Townsend Brown, an inventor he describes as building disc-shaped craft for the CIA, says that debris from a reported crash, discussed by the researcher Michael Swords, was analysed and found to be aluminum and barium. Michels points out that barium also appeared on a chalkboard at the Bahnson lab where Brown worked, and in Brown's Winterhaven proposal, a plan for building his craft, where Brown suggests barium for a motor in his "gravitator discs." If true, it would suggest the crashed object and Brown's secret designs were connected.
